references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1

u=\{f\in L^2(M,

Let $\mathcal H_T^0=\{u\in L^2(M,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0	ext{ for Lebesgue-almost every }\mathbf k\}$ with the second-variable-linear integral pairing. items.title: Transverse one-photon space and helicity projectors

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1
Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology, arXiv:2308.11147v2
Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Put $M=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega(\mathbf k)=|\mathbf k|$, and $d
u(\mathbf k)=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega(\mathbf k))$. Let $d\Omega$ denote polar surface measure on $S^2$. Polar coordinates give $d
u=(r/2)\,dr\,d\Omega$, and every orthogonal map preserves $
u$. The transverse one-photon Hilbert space $\mathcal H_T^
u$ consists of the equivalence classes $f\in L^2(M,
u;\mathbb C^3)$ satisfying $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ for $
u$-almost every $\mathbf k$, with pairing $\langle f,gangle_
u=\int_M\overline{f(\mathbf k)}\cdot g(\mathbf k)\,d
u(\mathbf k)$, linear in $g$. The preceding measure-isometry lemma gives the unitary $Wf(\mathbf k)=f(\mathbf k)/\sqrt{2\omega(\mathbf k)}$ from this space to the transverse space defined with measure $d^3\mathbf k$. The null set $\mathbf k=0$ is omitted throughout.

For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, define $P(\mathbf n)=I-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$. Extend the real cross product complex-linearly by $(\mathbf n	imes v)_i=\sum_{j,\ell=1}^3\epsilon_{ij\ell}n_jv_\ell$, where $\epsilon_{ij\ell}$ is totally antisymmetric and $\epsilon_{123}=1$, and set $h(\mathbf n)=i\,\mathbf n	imes$ and $P_\sigma(\mathbf n)=(P(\mathbf n)+\sigma h(\mathbf n))/2$ for $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Each $P_\sigma(\mathbf n)$ is a rank-one orthogonal projector on the complex transverse plane $P(\mathbf n)\mathbb C^3$, and $h$ has eigenvalue $\sigma$ on its range. The fibers $\mathcal L_{\sigma,\mathbf n}=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma(\mathbf n)$ form smooth complex line subbundles of $S^2	imes\mathbb C^3$. Here a smooth line subbundle means a family of one-dimensional complex fibers with smooth local unit sections. The common smooth domain for differential calculations is

$$\mathcal D=\{f\in C_c^\infty(M;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0	ext{ for every }\mathbf k\in M\}.$$

It is dense in $\mathcal H_T^
u$. For $0<r_0<r_1<\infty$, the mass-shell measure of the radial annulus is $
u(\{r_0\le|\mathbf k|\le r_1\})=\pi(r_1^2-r_0^2)$; in particular $
u$ is sigma-finite.

items.title: Transverse rotations preserve helicity and generate total angular momentum

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1
Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology, arXiv:2308.11147v2
Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $\hbar>0$, and use the transverse Hilbert space, helicity projectors, and dense domain $\mathcal D$ defined above. Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb R^3$. Let $SO(3)=\{R\in M_3(\mathbb R):R^TR=I,\det R=1\}$ with the topology inherited from the Frobenius matrix norm $\|A\|_F=(\sum_{i,j=1}^3|A_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$. For $R\in SO(3)$ define $U(R)f(\mathbf k)=R f(R^{-1}\mathbf k)$. Then $U$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation on $\mathcal H_T^\nu$, and $P_\sigma(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)\,U(R)=U(R)\,P_\sigma(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)$ for $\sigma=\pm1$. For a unit axis $\mathbf a$, put $R_{\mathbf a}(t)=\exp(t[\mathbf a]_\times)$, where $[\mathbf a]_\times v=\mathbf a\times v$, and define $(S_{\mathbf a})_{ij}=-i\sum_{\ell=1}^3a_\ell\epsilon_{\ell ij}$, $L_{\mathbf a}=-i\hbar\,(\mathbf a\times\mathbf k)\cdot\nabla_{\mathbf k}$, and $S_{\mathbf a}^{\mathrm{op}}=\hbar S_{\mathbf a}$. The unique self-adjoint Stone generator $J_{\mathbf a}$ specified by $U(R_{\mathbf a}(t))=\exp(-itJ_{\mathbf a}/\hbar)$ acts on $\mathcal D$ as $J_{\mathbf a}=L_{\mathbf a}+S_{\mathbf a}^{\mathrm{op}}$. This total generator preserves transversality, while its orbital and spin terms generally do not separately preserve the transverse space. The stated self-adjoint operators are the Stone generators; the differential expression is their restriction to $\mathcal D$.

items.title: Helicity line bundles have nonzero Chern number

references.title: Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology, arXiv:2308.11147v2
Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1

items.statement:
Orient $S^2$ outward, so its area form is $d\Omega=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\varphi$. In the spherical chart away from the poles let $\mathbf n=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$, $\mathbf e_\theta=(\cos\theta\cos\varphi,\cos\theta\sin\varphi,-\sin\theta)$, and $\mathbf e_\varphi=(-\sin\varphi,\cos\varphi,0)$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ set $e_\sigma=(\mathbf e_\theta+i\sigma\mathbf e_\varphi)/\sqrt2$, a local unit frame of the helicity line $\mathcal L_{\sigma,\mathbf n}$. With Hermitian pairing $\overline u\cdot v$, define the skew-Hermitian connection form $\omega_\sigma=e_\sigma^\dagger de_\sigma$, its curvature $\Omega_\sigma=d\omega_\sigma$, the real Berry connection $A_\sigma=-i e_\sigma^\dagger de_\sigma$, and $F_\sigma=dA_\sigma$. Then
$$A_\sigma=-\sigma\cos\theta\,d\varphi,\qquad F_\sigma=\sigma\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\varphi,\qquad \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=2\sigma.$$
Use the Chern-Weil convention $c_1(\mathcal L_\sigma)[S^2]=\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_{S^2}\Omega_\sigma$ for $\nabla=d+\omega_\sigma$; then $c_1(\mathcal L_\sigma)[S^2]=-2\sigma$. The north and south unit gauges $e_\sigma^N=e^{i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma$ and $e_\sigma^S=e^{-i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma$ have transition $e_\sigma^N=e^{2i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma^S$, of winding $2\sigma$ as $\varphi$ increases from $0$ to $2\pi$. Thus neither helicity line admits a global smooth unit section. This obstruction concerns each line separately and makes no nontriviality claim about the rank-two transverse complex bundle.

title: Photon helicity bundles and exact transverse rotations — Examples

items.title: A fixed Cartesian polarization is not a global transverse helicity frame

references.title: Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology, arXiv:2308.11147v2
Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1

items.statement: Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb R^3$. The constant Cartesian circular vectors $e_\sigma^0=(e_1+i\sigma e_2)/\sqrt2$, for $\sigma=\pm1$, form a transverse helicity frame for every nonzero momentum direction; consequently this fixed pair supplies a momentum-independent polarization factor on the transverse one-photon space.
